propers.name: Introit
propers.text:
Salus populi ego sum, dicit Dominus: de quacumque tribulatione clamaverint
ad me, exaudiam eos: et ero illorum Dominus in perpetuum. Attendite, popule
meus, legem meam: inclinate aurem vestram in verba oris mei. V. Gloria
Patri.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

The 1861 heads the formulary `XIX. SUNDAY after PENTECOST.` at printed p. 445 and sets the Latin `Salus populi ego sum` beside this English, so the target identity is shown by the book's own Latin. The body is the complete printed Introit -- antiphon, Psalm 77 verse and Glory cue -- because the 1962 target carries the verse and Gloria Patri; the page proof is the 2026-08-20 verify passage over artifact pages 454-455, and the psalm verse was read on the page on 2026-10-01 and agrees with the item's OCR layer. The drop capital `I AM` is set `I am` and the versicle glyph `V.`. The Cummiskey witness remains a pre-1955 lay hand missal; this row makes no broader recension claim.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Haec munera, quaesumus, Domine, quae oculis tuae majestatis offerimus,
salutaria nobis esse concede. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium
tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

The dated page-image verification passage and the separate tracked public-domain passage bind this body; the wording also agrees with the 2026-09-28 checked derivative. Tua nos, Domine, medicinalis operatio, et a nostris perversitatibus
clementer expediat, et tuis semper faciat inhaerere mandatis. Per Dominum.
